title: A Novel Stretching Platform for Applications in Cell and Tissue Mechanobiology
protocol: Resuspend fluorescent microspheres in isopropanol to enhance mixing in PDMS.
Pipette 500 μl of fluorescent microspheres into a microcentrifuge tube and centrifuge at 16,200 x g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant and add 500 μl of isopropanol to the microcentrifuge tube.
Vortex the mixture for 5 minutes.
Allow the vial to sit overnight in the dark to let large particles settle.
Carefully remove the supernatant to a clean microcentrifuge vial the next morning.
Weigh 0.5 g of curing agent and mix with six 15 μl additions of bead solution, vortexing for 1 minute between each addition.
Mix 10 g of PDMS with the 0.5 g of curing agent supplemented with fluorescent beads for at least 12 minutes.
Fabricate an SU-8 2050 cross-shaped mold using standard photolithography techniques.
Pour 400 mg of PDMS with beads into the cross-shaped mold using a transfer pipette.
Cure the PDMS in the mold for 2 hr at 80 °C.
Peel off the substrate from the mold after curing.
Air-plasma treat the substrate and 8 anchoring features for 30 sec at 30 W.
Pour droplets of PDMS (curing agent:PDMS with a ratio of 1:20) in a Petri dish to form approximately 4 mm diameter drops.
Cure the PDMS drops upside down for 2 hr at 80 °C.
Bind the anchoring features on each end of the substrate, 4 mm from the square shaped indent present on the substrate.
Wrap each end of the substrate around the grooved cylindrical part of the clamps and secure it in place with setscrews.
Screw the 4 clamps on the clamp holder.
Pour PDMS (ratio 1:20) using a disposable transfer pipette at the interface between the substrate and the grooved cylindrical part of the clamps.
Spread uncured PDMS around the grooved cylindrical part using a 1.5 mm hex key.
Pour PDMS (1:20) in the grooves until completely filled by capillary action.
Cure the assembly at 80 °C for 2 hr.
Air-plasma treat the whole assembly for 30 sec at 30 W to sterilize and functionalize the substrate.
Functionalize the area of the substrate where cells will be seeded with 1 ml of 0.02 M acetic acid supplemented with 16 μg/ml of rat-tail collagen at room temperature for 1 hr.
Rinse the substrate 3 times with phosphate buffer.
Let the substrate dry at room temperature for at least 10 min.

Add 40 μl of culture medium supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% penicillin-streptomycin containing 2,000 cells in the center portion of the substrate to cover an area of 1 cm2 (cell density: 20 cells/mm2).
Put the whole assembly in a standard cell culture incubator with the substrate facing up.
Add 30 μl of warm culture medium to the drop on the substrate every 45 min for 3 hr.
After 3 hr, flip the assembly into a Petri dish filled with fresh culture medium and incubate overnight.
Prepare HEPES-buffered salt solution (HBSS) daily, adjusting pH to 7.4.
Maintain cells on the microscope stage using HBSS.
Mount the set-up on an inverted phase contrast or fluorescent microscope.
Mount the clamp-substrate assembly on the BAXS platform and motors.
Fill the Petri dish inside the heater with HEPES buffer.
Prepare Krebs physiological solution by mixing 118.1 mM NaCl, 11.1 mM D-glucose, 25 mM NaHCO3, 4.7 mM KCl, 1.2 mM MgSO4, 1.2 mM KH2PO4, and 2.5 mM CaCl2.
Adjust the pH of Krebs solution to 7.4.
Oxygenate the Krebs solution with carbogen medical gas (95% O2/5% CO2) for 30 min.
Mount clamps of BAXS platform along with load cell beforehand.
Perform mouse euthanasia with inhalation of 99% CO2 in a Plexiglas chamber.
Open mouse abdomen and cut the thoracic aorta to bleed the mouse.
Remove the diaphragm, thoracic cage, and lung lobes.
Keep the heart attached to the aorta while removing it from the thoracic cavity.
Cut between the vessel and spine to remove the heart, aortic root, and thoracic aorta.
Immerse the heart and aorta in Krebs solution immediately after excision.
Wash the aorta in Krebs solution to remove any blood clots.
Remove connective tissue using micro-scissors, tweezers, and a surgical dissecting microscope.
Determine unloaded vessel dimensions with a calibrated microscope.
Cut an aortic ring of about 2 mm in length.
Measure the length of the 2 mm aortic ring using a calibrated microscope.
Place this segment aside in Krebs solution.
Cut another aortic ring as small as possible between each of the 2 mm segments.
Put the small segment on a microscope glass slide with the lumen facing up.
Measure the wall thickness of the small segment using a calibrated microscope setting.
Fill the Petri dish on the BAXS platform with Krebs solution.
Insert the 2 mm aorta ring segment on the pulling pins.
Prepare surgical instruments and the euthanized mouse for thoracic aorta isolation.
Make a longitudinal abdominal incision, remove the thoracic cage and lung lobes.
Carefully remove the aorta using the heart to manipulate tissue.
Place the heart and aorta in Krebs physiological solution.
Clean the aorta by removing all connective tissues.
Evaluate the precise length of each vessel segment using an inverse microscope and analysis program.
Measure the thickness of small aorta segments for assessment.
